body.statement: For every valid explicit unnested input list \(\boldsymbol\gamma\), the map \(\mathsf N\) is deterministic, runs in \(O(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) time, and produces a predecessor-only normalized list \(\boldsymbol\gamma^{\circ}\). For every \(f\in\mathfrak F\) and every term index \(j\), \(\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j(f)\}=\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j^{\circ}(f)\}\); hence the raw and normalized rational scores agree pointwise. Later-coordinate deletions use recursiveness, self-intervention simplification uses \(E(f,I)_i=I(i)\), and canonical ordering changes no intervention. Thus every subsequent runtime uses exactly the normalized context set \(\mathcal H\) without claiming that arbitrary nested syntax is accepted.
body.justification: This lemma makes the predecessor-only compiler interface an explicit value-preserving reduction rather than a silent syntactic assumption.
body.gap: The order-only response-signature literature permits general intervention atoms, while the continuation proof needs a normalized predecessor-only retained dialect; the exact preprocessing contract is not part of the equality-partition result.
body.consumer: Every compiler theorem can measure \(h\) on the smaller normalized context set while preserving the input query value.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a raw atom \(A=\{V_{i,I}=y\}\).  Let \(I_{\leq i}\) be the restriction of \(I\) to coordinates at most \(i\).  By \texttt{def:ordered-evaluation}, an induction on \(t=1,\ldots,i\) gives
\[
 E(f,I)_t=E(f,I_{\leq i})_t,
\]
because the recursion at coordinate \(t\) consults only intervention entries at coordinates at most \(t\) and response values on coordinates strictly below \(t\).  Thus deleting entries with index greater than \(i\) leaves the truth value of \(A\) unchanged.  If \(i\in\operatorname{dom}(I)\), the same definition gives
\[
 E(f,I)_i=I(i),
 \qquad
 \mathbf 1\{V_{i,I}=y\}=\mathbf 1\{I(i)=y\},
\]
so the self-intervention replacement is also pointwise valid.  Otherwise all retained intervention coordinates precede \(i\).  Sorting their encodings and coalescing repeated identical pairs does not change the partial map \(I\), hence does not change \(E(f,I)_i\).  Boolean simplification of the resulting truth constants preserves the value of the conjunction.  Applying these facts to every atom yields, for every \(f\in\mathfrak F\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\),
\[
 \mathbf 1\{\gamma_j(f)\}
 =\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j^{\circ}(f)\}.
\]
Multiplication by \(c_j\) and summation therefore give
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^r c_j\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j(f)\}
 =\sum_{j=1}^r c_j\mathbf 1\{\gamma_j^{\circ}(f)\}=g(f).
\]

It remains to justify the preprocessing bound rather than assume it.  Scan the explicit token stream once, validate each coordinate and value against the explicitly listed alphabets charged in the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\), discard a later-coordinate pair as soon as its index is read, and perform a stable radix ordering of retained integer coordinate encodings.  The radix work is linear in the total number of bits in those encodings.  A second scan coalesces identical adjacent pairs and simplifies constants.  A deterministic binary trie on the normalized context encodings constructs the distinct set \(\mathcal H\), again in time linear in the number of input and output bits.  No step emits more tokens than it reads.  By the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\), the total time is therefore \(O(N_{\mathrm{in}})\).  The operations are prescribed in source order with canonical coordinate ordering, so \(\mathsf N\) is deterministic.  The retained atoms are predecessor-only, and the argument used only explicit unnested atoms; it makes no claim about succinct nested syntax.
